tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (checking security of SageMaker setups), lists multiple explicit trigger contexts (notebooks, Studio domains, models, endpoints, training/processing jobs, Feature Store, Model Monitor, Model Registry, and example user questions), and includes a boundary case directing to another skill. It is a single well-structured paragraph, concise despite covering breadth.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to check whether their Amazon SageMaker AI setup is secure: a security assessment, audit, posture review or hardening check of notebooks, Studio domains, models, endpoints, training/processing jobs, Feature Store, Model Monitor or Model Registry, or asks about one SageMaker security setting, such as \"are my notebooks exposed to the internet?\"... For diagnosing one specific denied SageMaker call, use aiml-access-diagnostics instead."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (like what SageMaker or IAM are) and focuses on project-specific procedures, scope boundaries, and verifiability rules the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: **Owns** — *proactive, point-in-time security misconfiguration posture* of SageMaker resources... **Defers to `aiml-access-diagnostics`**

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/safety-critical parts (read-only guardrail, verify vs prescribe) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while scope and reporting sections explain rationale rather than micromanaging, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource... Treat every account as production unless told otherwise.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools/approaches for the same task as equal options; it specifies a single read-only API approach consistently.
tests.evidence: ONLY call `Describe*`, `List*`, `Get*`, `BatchGet*`, and equivalent read operations.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (confirm scope, resolve regions, run checks, assemble report, self-check) applicable to any SageMaker assessment request, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Determine which **accounts** are in scope (default primary; or named IDs / 'all accounts').
